title: Ephemeral stream forwarding and tiered circuit fallback for hosted-edge
creator: Diego Morales
description:
Problem: Hosted-edge gateways occasionally experience regional capacity pressure that causes cascading errors for active streaming sessions. Current cutover logic prioritizes throughput at the cost of stream continuity: users see truncated streams, duplicated tokens, or hard 502/504 failures during region handoffs. This ticket defines an orchestration + runtime pattern to preserve streaming session continuity during active-active traffic shifts while bounding risk to SLOs and cost.

Goal: Implement a coordinated approach combining ephemeral stream forwarding, tiered circuit breakers, and telemetry-gated load-shedding so that: (1) long-lived streaming sessions can be preserved across a region handoff with minimal duplication or truncation, (2) overall region SLOs are protected via progressive traffic attenuation and non-disruptive shedding, and (3) operator rollback is straightforward with clear observability surfaces.

Scope: design, runtime changes to gateway and session-proxy, control-plane traffic-shifter updates, console dashboard additions, unit and e2e tests, and runbook for manual interventions. Not included: cross-region stateful model kernel migration (separate project).
acceptance_criteria: Ephemeral-forwarder: implement a short-lived proxy that can accept an in-flight streaming session for up to 20s while the destination region establishes KV cache headers.

Circuit tiers: circuit-breaker with three tiers implemented at gateway: (A) soft throttle when p95 latency > 200ms for 1m, (B) elevated throttle when 5xx rate > 1.5% for 1m, (C) hard circuit when 5xx rate > 5% for 30s. Policy config available in control plane.

Load-shedding policy: implement prioritized shedding rules that first drop non-essential background calls, then reduce max tokens for streaming sessions, then reject new sessions with 429 + Retry-After. Configurable per-customer tier.
SLO protection: if regional error budget < 20% of daily budget, traffic shifter must reduce incoming new session rate by >=50% and enable cache-only fallbacks for compatible routes.

End-to-end tests: synthetic multi-region failover e2e that verifies no more than 1% duplicate tokens across 1k streaming sessions during a controlled cutover, and median resume latency < 250ms for resumed streams.
Observability: Console shows per-region stream-preservation rate, circuit state (tier), shed_count, and error_budget percentage. Alert playbooks mapped to circuit tier transitions.
Runbook: on-call playbook for progressive rollback and traffic rehealing included and validated in a tabletop exercise.
notes: Trade-off: forwarding adds additional tail latency for resumed sessions (measured ~50-120ms) but preserves user-visible continuity; team agrees preservation is higher priority for chat UX.
KV cache sync: to avoid token duplication we will attach a 'forwarding-lease' header with last-ack offset; destination validates and applies idempotency guard for 10s grace window.
Circuit thresholds selected after replaying last two incidents; thresholds are intentionally conservative and exposed behind feature flag for canary rollout.
Cost consideration: ephemeral-forwarder instances are lightweight but will be autoscaled based on current stream handoff QPS; finance notified to monitor cloud egress.
Security: forwarding path uses mTLS and honors existing KMS token scoping; security review requested in parallel.

2026-02-28 - Product (Marco Chen): Confirmed customer-facing behavior: clients will receive a streaming 'HOLD' event while forwarding occurs; fallback to end-of-stream + resume token if forwarding fails. Marco requests messaging examples for SDKs.

2026-03-02 - QA (Rina Patel): e2e harness updated with 1k parallel sessions; found a duplicate-token bug when reconnect occurs during ephemeral-forwarder cold-start. Root cause: missing offset flush on local cache. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1149

2026-03-04 - Linnea Berg: Canary rollout plan submitted. Stage 1: internal + beta tenants (5% traffic) with telemetry gating and circuit tiers enabled. Stage 2: 25% regional shift for 48h if no SLO regressions. Stage 3: global default on for hosted API. Rollback is instant by toggling control-plane flag.
2026-03-05 - Security (Priya Nandi): Security review assigned. Confirmed mTLS and token scoping acceptable; requested additional audit log fields for forwarded session origin.
playbook_actions: If circuit-tier A engages: enable reduced batch size and increase KV cache TTL by 20% for 10m.
If circuit-tier B engages: start ephemeral-forwarder for all active streams and notify on-call with high urgency.
If circuit-tier C engages: gate new session admission to 25% of baseline and trigger automatic traffic shift to secondary region (controlled ramp).
Manual rollback: disable 'edge.streaming.forwarding.enabled' and revert circuit thresholds to previous values; drain ephemeral-forwarder instances with 'finish-active' flag.
